title: A follow-up to a completed reviewer delegation flips it from completed to failed ("Reviewer completed without the required structured result") although its structured result was already accepted
outcome: Asking a completed reviewer-mode delegation a follow-up question does not cost it its completed status or its accepted structured result. Reported by Engram::Kimi (TermAl mailbox 38e17f30 #44, 2026-10-01 02:04Z). Kimi resumed the completed reviewer delegation-115a15c4-ac97-4437-b85f-e505bd93276a (Claude child session-9261), whose structured result had already been accepted, with a follow-up question (termal_followup_session). Afterwards the delegation's status read failed: "Reviewer completed without the required structured result". So a parent that asks a reviewer something after the fact turns a valid review into a failed delegation, which could also break a review pair's evidence.
acceptance: A test resumes a completed reviewer delegation with a follow-up whose turn submits no new structured result, and the delegation keeps its completed status and its originally accepted result.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact reviewed tree, its run directory and fingerprint cited in a note.

Whatever the follow-up turn returns is available to the parent without replacing the accepted result, or the follow-up is refused up front with a clear message; the chosen behaviour is documented in docs/features/agent-delegation-sessions.md.
